slots.name: ACS sample individuals
slots.sentence: The 2023 ACS includes a representative sample of approximately 3,400,000 individuals in approximately 1,500,000 households, corresponding to about 1% of the population and including unauthorized immigrants.

slots.name: ACS sample households
slots.sentence: The 2023 ACS includes a representative sample of approximately 3,400,000 individuals in approximately 1,500,000 households, corresponding to about 1% of the population and including unauthorized immigrants.

slots.name: Medicaid measure gap
slots.sentence: The effect is largest for Medicaid: at the individual level, non-citizens use it at about the same rate as U.S.-born citizens, but counting a household as a beneficiary when one member participates opens a roughly 20-point gap, making non-citizens appear to use the program far more.

slots.name: Medicaid underreporting
slots.sentence: A substantial literature comparing survey responses to administrative records finds that program participation in benefits including SNAP and Medicaid is frequently under-reported, with roughly one-third of true SNAP recipients and one in five Medicaid participants in the ACS failing to report participation.

slots.name: Cato 2023 benefit gap
slots.sentence: Cato finds that, on a per capita basis, immigrants consumed 24 percent less welfare and entitlement benefits than native-born Americans in 2023, while CIS finds that, in 2024, 53% of households headed by immigrants used one or more major welfare programs compared to 37% for U.S.-born households.

slots.name: Cato 2022 benefit gap
slots.sentence: Cato estimates that immigrants used 21% less welfare and entitlement benefits than native-born Americans on a per capita basis in 2022, while CIS finds that 54% of households headed by immigrants used at least one major welfare program in 2022, compared to 39% for U.S.-born households.
